title: Tamsin and the Hollow
premise: Tamsin Blackwood, last apprentice of the Wardens of the Hollow, lives in a valley where magic cannot cross the boundary stones. When a mute child arrives speaking the dead tongue of Caelmere—a country erased from every map and memory—Tamsin learns her guild once helped unmake that nation, and that the child is its living remnant, hunted by the winter itself. To save her, Tamsin must leave the valley for the first time, find the door back into a country that no longer exists, and choose between exposing her guild's buried crime and preserving the only family she has left. In the end she opens the door, lets Caelmere's people pass through into the world's memory again, and burns the guild's charter—finding belonging not in an institution but in the truth she refuses to abandon.
about_author: Ansel Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the records of defunct institutions before turning to fiction. They write about forgotten places and the people stubborn enough to remember them.

chapters.title: The Boundary Stones
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She tends the valley's boundary stones with her dying master, Aldous, chafing at a guild that has shrunk to two members and endless ritual. A child appears at the gate in the first snowfall, speaking a language no one should know. The beat is quiet unease—the ordinary world cracking open.

chapters.title: A Tongue Before Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The child, whom Tamsin names Wren, cannot speak any living language, but Aldous goes pale when he hears her: it is Old Caelmerish, the tongue of a country struck from history. He forbids Tamsin from asking how the girl crossed the stones. Beat: protective curiosity curdling into suspicion of her own master.

chapters.title: What the Charter Keeps
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, with a letter from Aldous's POV woven in. Searching the guild archive for the word 'Caelmere,' Tamsin finds pages razored out of the founding charter—and realizes the excision was recent. Aldous burns correspondence in the hearth. Beat: the first hard evidence that her family's legacy is built on something hidden.

chapters.title: The Winter That Follows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, rendered in close third. Snow falls upward at the boundary; frost writes words only Wren can read. She remembers, in fragments, a city of glass bridges and the night it was 'closed.' Something vast and cold is walking toward the valley. Beat: dread made intimate through a child's memory.

chapters.title: The Third Warden
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A stranger arrives claiming to be a Warden from a branch lodge Tamsin has never heard of, demanding the child be surrendered 'for containment.' Aldous backs him. Tamsin lies for the first time in her life, hiding Wren in the crypt beneath the chapel. Beat: loyalty and truth pull apart for the first time.

chapters.title: Confession at the Hearth
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. Dying, he tells Tamsin the truth: the Wardens did not guard magic from the valley—they guarded the valley from what they did to Caelmere, sealing a whole nation behind the stones to end a war their charter signed. Wren is what escaped. Beat: grief and betrayal braided together; the mentor becomes the accused.

chapters.title: Over the Stones
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. With Aldous dead and the false Warden hunting them, Tamsin crosses the boundary carrying Wren—and magic floods into her like cold water, terrifying and alive. Outside, the world is mid-winter and wrong, roads ending in fields that remember being cities. Beat: awe and homesickness in a single breath.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Alternating Tamsin and Wren POVs. Following Wren's fragmentary memories, they reach the place where Caelmere's capital stood: a hollow in the world where nothing casts a shadow. The false Warden corners them and reveals the guild's plan—to let the long winter finish falling and bury the crime forever. Beat: rising tension peaks; the antagonist's logic is almost persuasive.

chapters.title: The Door Out
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the heart of the hollow stands the door out of Caelmere, sealed by the same oath that erased the country. Opening it requires a name spoken in the old tongue and a truth spoken aloud in the new. Tamsin confesses her guild's crime to the listening dark, and the lock turns. Beat: climax—truth as the literal key.

chapters.title: After the Long Winter
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The door opens onto spring: Caelmere's survivors step back into the world, and maps redraw themselves overnight. Tamsin returns to the valley, burns the charter, and raises Wren among neighbors who now remember a country they'd lost. Beat: resolution—belonging rebuilt on truth rather than silence, justice done outside any law.
